text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Electricity prices on the Norwegian and Swedish power bourse have fallen by 20 percent since the end of September due to a lot of rain in western Norway, reducing fears of a power crisis this winter.

- A Russian military aircraft sniffed low, passing the Norwegian offshore oil platform Heidrun at a distance of 1,000 feet a month ago. A Defence Ministry spokesman confirmed the incident, which upset oilworkers, but said no action would be taken because the plane was flying in international airspace.
- Statoil is looking into the shipping and offshore service industry as part of considerations to possibly spin off the shipping activities of the state-owned oil company.

- Norway's largest insurer, Storebrand, wants to reduce costs. The employees have been asked by company president Age Korsvold to present plans for how to reduce cost by at least 40 percent, equivalent to savings of nearly 500 million crowns.

- Hydro Texaco will spend 200 million crowns on changing to a more enviromentally friendly profile of the company's 430 petrol stations in Norway. Hydro Texaco's petrol stations have been called the country's ugliest petrol stations by Culture Minister Ase Kleveland.
